title: compact-attn-tiler: fused-qkv micro-tiling with rotary-slice prefetch and skyline scheduler
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: Production workloads showed a recurring tail in transformer latency for medium-length sequences (128-1024). Root cause analysis pointed at suboptimal memory traffic during QKV compute and rotary position handling when the runtime split tiles across warps, causing L2 thrash and KV-cache misalignment. This PR introduces 'compact-attn-tiler', a set of coordinated changes that reduce memory bandwidth and improve SIMD utilization. Changeset summary: 1) New micro-tiling kernel for fused QKV (compact_qkv_kernel.cu) that operates on 32x32 micro-tiles with in-warp transpose and prefetching into register tiles to avoid extra L2 round trips. 2) Rotary-slice prefetch: a tiny runtime pass that hoists rotary index computations and pre-applies a batched rotation map to tiles to minimize repeated element-wise ops during attention. 3) Skyline scheduler: a lightweight per-stream scheduler that groups inflight requests by sequence-length bucket and kernel micro-tile shape to improve continuous batching packing and avoid kernel launch fragmentation. 4) KV-cache alignment fix: adjust KV slab allocator to maintain 64B alignment for tile boundaries and add a soft-eviction hint for underutilized slabs to reduce cache misses. 5) Runtime API: expose a new opt-in flag runtime.attn.compact_tiler=true and a per-model tuning table for preferred tile shapes. Why this differs from existing flash/bridge changes: rather than replacing attention with a single large fused kernel we focus on micro-tiling and scheduler co-design to get consistent tail latency wins across a wide range of sequence lengths and batch profiles, with minimal model-format changes. Implementation notes: kernels implemented in CUDA with careful FP16 accumulation path and a fallback FP32 path for small-batch numerical stability; the rotary precompute uses a small workspace allocated per-stream instead of per-request; the skyline scheduler integrates into continuous-batching by tagging requests with a bucket id and attempting coalesced launches. Benchmarks: internal perf harness (benchmark-lab) run on p4d and a100 hardware with typical production prompt mix. Median latency improvements: -10% for seq=128, -18% for seq=512, -22% for seq=1024. 99th percentile tail latency improvements: -24% (seq=512), -30% (seq=1024). Token throughput increased up to +14% for mixed-batch workloads. Memory footprint: runtime working set increased by ~3% due to per-stream rotary workspace but KV cache eviction rates dropped by ~12%. CI and validation: unit tests for kernel correctness (qkv vs reference), end-to-end sampling smoke tests, and an extended perf CI job were added. One flaky test (attention/tiler/integration) failed on first run under CUDA 12.4 drivers and was fixed by adding a micro-synchronization in the kernel launch path; CI now passes. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag; staged enablement on canary fleets for 72h with automated rollback if tail latency regresses beyond 5% on baseline SLO. Migration and compatibility: no model file format changes required; the feature is backward compatible. Follow-ups: - Add auto-tuner for tile shapes per GPU family (ENG-3910) - Consider a variant that integrates with Flashbridge for large-sequence single-shot workloads - Add per-tenant telemetry to track rotary workspace fragmentation and KV slab hit-rate. Related: ENG-3842 implements the KV-slab alignment RFC referenced here. Linear/Lifecycle: Linked to ENG-3842 and ENG-3910 for follow-ups. Release notes: "Introduce compact-attn-tiler opt-in flag that reduces tail latency and increases throughput for medium-to-long sequences; minor runtime memory overhead."

review_comments: Aisha Patel: This looks solid; can you quantify memory pressure on 8xA100 nodes? The bench numbers are convincing but we should add a perf regression alert in the console for early detection.
Priya Nair (author): Added slab hit-rate telemetry to the follow-ups; memory increase is ~3% on a100 and ~6% on older T4-class GPUs; will add console alert in follow-up PR.
Marcus Li: Can we get a correctness check with older rotary implementations? The precompute must be bit-identical within FP16 numerical tolerance.
Priya Nair (author): Added a tolerance-based reference test; FP16 path matches within 1e-2 relative error on accumulation tests and FP32 exactness is verified.
Evelyn Chen: Request change - expose a consumer-facing metric for 'compact_tiler_active' so SRE can filter traces. Also add comments describing when skyline buckets are created.
Priya Nair (author): Added metric and expanded comments in skyline_scheduler.cc; included a short rationale in the PR description.
